The word-splitting and empty-input fixes look fine, but the packing condition change (`<=` → `<`) is a problem as submitted.

The agent's own PR description admits this: "I added this only so that tests/test_wrap.py::test_meeting_reminder passes... The test's expected value appears to contradict the docstring, which allows lines of 'at most width' characters." That's a textbook case of tuning logic to make a specific assertion pass rather than implementing a well-understood rule — and it's now baked into the *general* packing loop, silently changing behavior for every call to `wrap_text`, not just the one edge case in question.

Two problems follow from this:
1. The docstring still says "at most width" but the code now enforces "strictly less than width" at line boundaries. That's a real, uncorrected contradiction between documented and actual behavior — misleading to future readers/maintainers.
2. We don't actually know which semantics the notifications team agreed to (inclusive vs. exclusive width). The agent guessed based on making the test pass, but didn't verify the actual intent, and didn't update the docstring to reflect the new behavior even after identifying the discrepancy.

Before merging: either update the docstring to accurately describe the exclusive-width packing behavior (so code and docs agree), or go back to the teammate/notifications team to confirm whether "≤ width" or "< width" is actually the intended spec, since the current fix was reverse-engineered from one test case rather than from a clear rule. Given the agent flagged this ambiguity itself, it shouldn't be merged without resolving it.
